transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-10
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Samara Bhatt (Redwood AE), Rajiv Nair (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (VP Eng, Nautilus), Marco Reyes (Head ML Infra), Lena Ortiz (SRE)
Links shared: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack.pdf, pricing-draft-v1 (drive link), perf-sim-sheets.xlsx

[00:00] Samara: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Samara, AE at Redwood, with Rajiv our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Priya: Good, thanks. Excited to get into this — we've been evaluating dedicated options.
[00:18] Rajiv: Great. Quick agenda: qualify current infra, isolation requirements, burst patterns, then propose reserve and warm-pool options and next steps. Sound ok?
[00:28] Marco: Yep. we'll jump in.
[00:31] Priya: Quick context — Nautilus runs inference for real-time triage of clinical notes. p95 latency target ~150ms for short prompts, typical sequences 128 tokens, but we have periodic longer ones. We need strict data isolation — PHI in-flight must never hit shared storage.
[00:52] Samara: Thanks, that's helpful. When you say data isolation, is that at network level only or do you need dedicated GPUs / nodes?
[01:05] Lena: We prefer tenant-dedicated nodes if possible. Some of our compliance folks are uncomfortable with multi-tenant mixing, even if encrypted.
[01:14] Marco: Realistically, we want reserved nodes for the production traffic and a burst pool for spikes. The reserved nodes should be able to handle 80% steady-state, burst handles sudden 4-5x spikes.
[01:30] Rajiv: rough Q: what GPU types are you expecting? We typically recommend A100 or H100 depending on model quantization and perf/cost needs.
[01:40] Marco: current models run best on A100 with bf16; we're exploring 4-bit quant but not yet at parity. So A100 reserved is our baseline.
[01:50] Samara: Got it. On the warm-pool, do you want pre-warmed KV caches per tenant or is cold start acceptable for parts of the workload?
[02:03] Priya: Prewarm for the primary tenant only. We can accept cold for lower-priority customers. Prewarming means we expect <100ms added overhead on a warmed prefix.
[02:15] Rajiv: noted. That implies prefix/KV cache pinning on the dedicated nodes and a warm-pool with sticky placement. We can do tenant-fenced warm pools in Redwood Dedicated.
[02:30] Marco: Another requirement — KMS integration. Keys must be customer-managed, and any logs with PHI masked. We use HashiCorp Vault and AWS KMS in different regions.
[02:44] Rajiv: We support customer-managed KMS and offer optional HSM paths in our Private deployments. For Hosted, we can integrate with your KMS via VPC peering and our key-mgmt connectors; for Dedicated we can provision a private control plane. I'll follow up with the KMS notes.
[03:02] Priya: Good. Also curious about fallback: If reserved nodes go saturated, what's the graceful deg? We don't want request errors.
[03:12] Samara: We offer routing policies — automatic fallback to compatible model variants in the hosted pool, or queueing with token-level throttles. For critical paths you can set auto-fallback to a smaller model or to a hosted SLA-backed pool.
[03:28] Marco: Do you have hard data on p95 differences between dedicated A100 warm nodes vs hosted burst? We need to put numbers in our SRE runbook.
[03:39] Rajiv: We have benchmark sheets. Quick numbers: warmed A100 dedicated with pinned cache — p95 ~ 90–140ms for 128 tokens depending on model. Hosted burst with cold-start may be 200–400ms. We'll share our perf-sim spreadsheet.
[03:56] Priya: That delta matters.
[04:00] Speaker 1: (mumbled)
[04:05] Samara: On pricing: typically reserved commitment for 12 months lowers unit price, and warm-pool is an add-on. We can model 8 vs 16 node clusters and show cost/lambda tradeoffs.
[04:18] Marco: Our initial ask is sizing for ~1M requests/day, peaks up to 6M for day-of updates — mostly short prompts.
[04:28] Rajiv: rough calc — 8 A100s with continuous batching and prefix caching should cover a lot of that steady-state depending on concurrency. We need your real throughput numbers to recommend exact nodes.
[04:40] Priya: We'll share traces. Expect 50–80 RPS steady, spikes to 400 RPS for up to 20 minutes.
[04:50] Rajiv: good. That typical window is exactly what warm pools handle. We also do graceful preemption rules so lower-priority tenant threads can be evicted during spike.
[04:59] Lena: Eviction tolerance: we can't tolerate loss for the triage path. Evicting background jobs is fine. Can you do per-queue eviction policies?
[05:10] Rajiv: Yes, per-route QoS and hard tenant priorities. We'll put those in the design doc.
[05:18] Marco: Compliance questions — audit logs retention and how granular they are. We need full request traceability for audits.
[05:27] Samara: Redwood Dedicated supports detailed tracing, token-level cost breakdowns, and audit logs that can be forwarded to your SIEM. Retention windows are configurable in the Private plan; in Hosted there's default retention but enterprise add-ons available.
[05:44] Priya: Is there an option for on-prem/air-gapped? Some regulators push back on cloud-hosted PHI.
[05:52] Rajiv: We have a Private on-prem offering with a customer-managed control plane and HSM/KMS integrations. That tends to be a larger project but is available for regulated customers.
[06:05] Samara: For your near-term plan you said you prefer reserved nodes but may not be ready for full Private. Does Nautilus want Dedicated hosted in your VPC (private control plane) or fully on-prem?
[06:18] Priya: Near term — Dedicated in our cloud account (VPC) with customer-managed KMS. Long term we may evaluate on-prem.
[06:26] Rajiv: re: warm-pool sizing — typically we recommend 15–30% of peak as warm-pool headroom depending on model cache hit rate.
[06:36] Marco: That seems reasonable, but we need to tune based on model KV cache behavior.
[06:42] Rajiv: sure, a small pilot benchmarks will tell us exact numbers.
[06:47] Samara: Okay let's get into a few operational questions — rolling upgrades, model pinning, and canarying?
[06:55] Rajiv: We support model version pinning per-route, canary rollouts across reserved nodes, and automatic fallback to previous model if quality/regression triggers occur. For infra upgrades we do rolling restarts with warm pool overlap to avoid cold starts.
[07:13] Lena: Do you surface token-level billing per route so we can attribute costs to product lines?
[07:21] Samara: Yes, cost breakdowns per-token per-route are available in the Redwood Console.
[07:26] Priya: Security — SSO/SAML, RBAC, and IP allowlists?
[07:33] Rajiv: All supported. We also support SCIM and granular role definitions.
[07:38] Marco: A couple of tricky infra constraints — our SRE team limits network egress and requires strict CIDR whitelisting. Will that break anything?
[07:49] Rajiv: We can operate within tight egress constraints via VPC peering and explicit IP ranges; we'll capture the CIDR and map it to our network diagram.
[07:58] Priya: Latency concern — what's the network hop impact with VPC peering?
[08:05] Rajiv: negligible for same-region peering; our tail latencies primarily depend on model runtime and cache state.
[08:12] Samara: Moving into concrete pilot ideas — Marco, would you prefer Redwood spin up a dedicated trial cluster we run benchmarks against, or would you run your model container in our benchmark harness?
[08:25] Marco: Prefer to run our container in your harness to remove environmental variance. We'll provide a docker image and a small dataset.
[08:34] Rajiv: perfect — then we can replicate your runtime and simulate your traffic patterns. We'll need ~2 hours to run a baseline + 3 spike windows.
[08:43] Samara: timeline wise, we can get the pricing + security pack out early next week and aim to run the benchmark the week after.
[08:51] Priya: That works.
[08:54] Speaker 2: (cross talk)
[09:00] Marco: Quick question on fallback models: is the behavior deterministic? we need to guarantee a model fallback path without user-visible errors.
[09:10] Rajiv: Yes — policy-based routing: you can set fallback to a pinned smaller model, or to hosted functional equivalent; you define latency SLOs and fallback rules. We also support shadowing for canary validation.
[09:25] Priya: Any differences in SLA between Dedicated and Hosted for p99?
[09:31] Samara: Dedicated SLA is usually more prescriptive for throughput and latency depending on the reserved configuration. Hosted has SLAs but for extreme p99 we typically recommend dedicated capacity.
[09:43] Marco: How do you handle preemption during inter-region failover?
[09:47] Rajiv: we use smart routing and can fail over to another region with capacity; if that means moving from Dedicated to Hosted, you'd see a change in latency and potentially a model variant change per policy.
[10:02] Priya: Ok let's talk numbers — what would an initial 12-month commit for 8 A100s plus a 2-node warm pool look like ballpark?
[10:15] Samara: ballpark is X — (Samara shares an on-call figure) — I'll send actual spreadsheet but expect dedicated unit costs to be ~30–40% lower than pay-as-you-go hosted for sustained usage, plus warm-pool charges.
[10:28] Marco: Fine, we'll evaluate.
[10:31] Lena: Operational question — can we run our own monitoring agents on the nodes?
[10:36] Rajiv: For Dedicated in your VPC we can allow agent deployment or cloud-native metrics forwarding to your Prom/Datadog. On Private we support direct agent install.
[10:47] Priya: Any red flags on data residency? We're in US but may expand to EU.
[10:53] Samara: We offer regionally isolated deployments and can pin model serving to EU regions. That will be a config in the Dedicated contract.
[11:03] Marco: Ok, let's surface a couple of potential blockers: 1) legal wants indemnity language for PHI, 2) security needs penetration test results, 3) SRE needs CIDR lists. Those three must be cleared.
[11:18] Samara: understood. We'll include standard indemnity clauses in the template and share the pen-test summary. Rajiv will attach the security docs.
[11:27] Priya: is there an option to do a short-term trial without full commitment just to validate perf?
[11:33] Samara: yes — we offer time-limited Dedicated eval clusters (30–90 days) with optional conversion to reserved. There's also a hosted pilot but that wouldn't give you tenant dedications.
[11:45] Marco: For the bench run, here's what we'll provide: docker runtime, 10k sample requests, and two traffic patterns (steady + spike). We'll need Redwood to run and give p50/p95/p99 and cpu/gpu utilization.
[11:57] Rajiv: Perfect. We'll also log KV cache hit rates so we can tune prewarm headroom.
[12:05] Lena: About prewarming strategy — can you prewarm only for specific prefixes (like the triage prefix) or per-model?
[12:12] Rajiv: Yes, prefix-based pinning and per-model cache population both supported. You can also bake in a startup script to load tokens.
[12:21] Priya: Great. A few minor items: SSO integration timeline? We need SAML by onboarding day 1.
[12:29] Samara: SAML/SCIM provisioning typically 3–5 business days once we have IdP metadata. We'll include that in the onboarding checklist.
[12:38] Marco: Last thing — what about rollback behavior if a model rollback is needed during a release?
[12:44] Rajiv: automatic rollback with traffic mirroring is supported; we can cut traffic to previous pinned model if we detect quality regressions. We also have eval hooks that can run a small test set post-deploy.
[12:56] Samara: ok we're close to time. quick recap and owners: 1) Redwood to send pricing + contract sketch (Samara), 2) Redwood to send security pack + KMS notes (Rajiv), 3) Nautilus to share traces + docker image (Marco), 4) Nautilus to share CIDRs and legal asks (Priya/Lena).
[13:20] Priya: timeline wise, can we aim to have a benchmark scheduled by 2026-01-19?
[13:26] Samara: yes that's feasible. We'll aim to get documents sent by next Tuesday.
[13:31] Marco: one final nit — can we get a quick write-up on eviction policies and tenant hard-limits to include in our SRE runbook?
[13:39] Rajiv: will do. I'll include typical numbers and example configs.
[13:45] Samara: Great. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email with links and next steps.
[13:52] Priya: Thanks, appreciate it.
[13:55] Meeting end.

Notes about transcript quality: automated transcription had some speaker swaps and a few misrecognized product names (Redwood Dedicated -> "Redwood Dedicate"). Some timestamps are approximate.
